sources.title: Bring the match in.
sources.lead: Events and video share one analysis pipeline. Model API access remains separately authorized.
sources.events_intro: Import MatchLens JSONL to replay its event clock. Live sources can use /api/ingest; repeated messages are not counted twice.
sources.video_intro: Local pretrained models detect players and the ball, track motion and infer events without training. Pitch landmarks are automatic or manually corrected. Video stays on this computer. Wide, continuous shots work best; occlusions and cuts interrupt measurement.
sources.calibration_intro: Automatic calibration uses pretrained landmarks. For manual correction, choose at least four non-collinear points in the first frame and their corresponding coordinates on a 105 × 68 m pitch. Use the button below to pick points. This calibrates the pitch; it does not label passes or shots.
sources.pick: Pick a point in the frame
sources.identity_help: You can edit the configuration. identities binds track IDs to known names and shirt numbers; unbound tracks stay anonymous. Provide team_directions (for example A:1, U:-1) and initial_score when known. Unknown directions and scores remain unconfirmed; shots are not inferred without direction. Start a new calibrated clip after a camera cut.

lab.intro: This experiment uses color classification and temporal rules to estimate player positions, passes, possession changes, shots and ball speed from video pixels. It reads frames, not the generator’s event labels.
lab.scope: A fixed overhead view with a full 105 × 68 m pitch, 22 identity colors and a white ball. This is a classical vision baseline; broadcast occlusion, camera motion and shirt recognition require pretrained vision models.
lab.method_text: Identity uses preset colors and position uses pixel centers. Reception needs two consecutive near-ball frames with ball speed below 3 m/s. The largest connected region filters encoding noise. Free ball motion between owners indicates a pass; an opponent reception indicates interception and possession change. Speed is planar displacement over time. A shot is a trajectory estimate toward the goal line and does not confirm a goal. Missing or skipped frames reset state without inventing motion. Outputs are labeled classical_vision_estimate.
